clue.text: Flustered chairmen went to vintner

indicators.note: flustered means agitated and thrown into disorder, so the letters of the next two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Agitated company directors visit a wine seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flustered' looks like it describes the chairmen, but it is the anagram signal for CHAIRMEN and WENT together.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintner is a person who sells wine by trade.

clue.text: Insinuated that mischievous child told a fib

parts.note: an imp is a naughty child
lied means told a fib

explanation.surface: Someone hinted that a naughty kid had been untruthful.
explanation.definitionFit: To insinuate is to hint at something without stating it outright.

clue.text: Disorder puts private investigator in sleepy confusion

indicators.note: in places the detective inside the other letters
confusion means a muddle, so the letters of sleepy are mixed up

explanation.surface: An illness throws a drowsy detective into a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'confusion' as a symptom of the disorder, but it signals the anagram; 'in' marks the container, and 'puts' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Epilepsy is a neurological condition causing seizures, a medical disorder.

clue.text: Therefore sends monster back

indicators.note: sending the word back means writing it backwards

parts.note: an ogre is a monster

explanation.surface: A logical conclusion: so the monster is sent packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns OGRE round; 'sends' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for hence, used in English to draw a logical conclusion.

clue.text: Company boxing cereal cultivates heraldic insignia

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the company wraps around the cereal

parts.note: oat is a cereal crop
to farm land is to cultivate it

explanation.surface: An agricultural firm that packages grain and works the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' reads as a sport beside 'Company', but here it means enclosing, so the cereal goes inside the firm's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A family's heraldic design on a shield is its armorial bearing or crest.

clue.text: Beer is found inside part of church

indicators.note: is found inside means the word is goes within the beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone discovers beer stashed in a section of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found inside' marks a container; the surface imagines beer discovered in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A church's passage between the pews, or a side section of the nave.

clue.text: B4 U worry, start enjoying being 13 to 19

parts.note: the letter before U in the alphabet is T, spelt out as tee
to nag is to worry or pester someone

indicators.note: start means take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Text-speak advice to a youngster: before you fret, start enjoying your teens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'B4 U' is text-speak for 'before U': the letter preceding U is T, written as its name TEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being from thirteen to nineteen is being in one's teens, at an adolescent age.

clue.text: "Come on Petunia"-might be how story starts

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters could form something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale opening that could be someone encouraging Petunia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' rearranges COME ON PETUNIA; the quotation marks make the surface a line of dialogue.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional opening formula of a fairy tale.

clue.text: Looking youthful, comfortable, quiet and reticent

parts.note: well off, comfortable financially
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
reserved means reticent

explanation.surface: A description of someone ageing nicely: comfortable, quiet and self-contained.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for piano, the musical direction meaning play quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks young for their age is said to have kept themselves in good condition.

clue.text: Having forty winks; don't start speaking in abrupt tone

indicators.note: telling the word not to start means its opening letter is dropped

parts.note: snapping is speaking sharply and irritably

explanation.surface: Someone dozing is told off for barking at people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't start' removes the S at the front of SNAPPING.
explanation.definitionFit: Forty winks is a short sleep, so someone having it is dozing lightly.

clue.text: Stern arrangement of features, not feminine

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
not signals that the letter for feminine is left out of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written
F is the standard abbreviation for feminine in grammar

explanation.surface: A severe face, its features set with nothing womanly about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops F from FEATURES, leaving EATURES, and 'arrangement of' shuffles those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a severe, unsmiling manner with no softness or indulgence.

clue.text: The Israelites sheltered a chosen group

indicators.note: something sheltered is kept within, so the answer lies inside the run of letters of these words

explanation.surface: A biblical remark that the Israelites gave refuge to God's chosen people.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across IsraELITEs; 'Israelites' points to 'chosen people' to blur the definition into the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An elite is a select, privileged set of people picked out as the best.

clue.text: Violated dislocated joint

indicators.note: dislocated means put out of place, so the letters of the word before are moved around

explanation.surface: An injured, put-out joint described as having been violated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dislocated' seems part of a medical scene about a joint, but it rearranges VIOLATED.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is a woodworking joint of interlocking wedge-shaped tenons.

clue.text: Equip elderly university tutor for ultimate battle

parts.note: to arm is to equip with weapons
aged means elderly
a don is a tutor at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Arming an old academic for the final war.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, the final battle between good and evil at the end of the world.

clue.text: Person without transport lacks imagination

definitions.meaning: someone travelling on foot rather than by vehicle
the adjective sense: dull, plodding and uninspired, as the clue's phrase describes

explanation.definitionFit: A walker goes on foot; as an adjective the word means dull and prosaic, plodding like a walker.

clue.text: Split number from visionary

indicators.note: taking a number from a word means removing it

parts.note: to sever is to split or cut apart
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Breaking up with a numbers person to go with a dreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes V (Roman five) out of SEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A visionary is a prophet who foresees the future.

clue.text: Cares not about forefather

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the letters of cares and not are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone unconcerned about their predecessors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cares not about' reads as indifference, but 'about' shuffles CARES and NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A forefather is a person from whom one is descended.

clue.text: Almost darkness but not quite

indicators.note: not quite the whole word means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: night is the time of darkness

explanation.surface: It is nearly dark, though not completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' takes the final T off NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old word for near, so it means nearly.

clue.text: Give access to small stream for a great ape

parts.note: a go is a turn or chance, an opening granted to someone
a rill is a small stream or brook

explanation.surface: Opening a brook to a large primate.
explanation.walkthrough: GO for 'Give access to' is loose: a go is a turn or chance, the opening granted. RILL is a little-used word for a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest primate, a powerful African ape.

clue.text: Ill-breeding generates Spooner's insane military standards

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words, so the opening letters of the two pieces change places

parts.note: mad means insane
banners are flags carried as standards by an army

explanation.surface: Coarse upbringing produces regimental flags that are crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the openings of MAD BANNERS gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-breeding is rude, uncouth behaviour showing poor upbringing.

clue.text: Deeply instil earning potential

indicators.note: potential means what something could become, so the letters may be formed into another word

explanation.surface: Instilling a sense of one's earning power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' rearranges EARNING.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix a habit or belief firmly in someone, working it into their nature like a grain in wood.

clue.text: Rob a small pasty

definitions.meaning: a slang phrase for raiding or ransacking a place
a pastry folded over a sweet filling, such as apple

explanation.definitionFit: Burglars ransacking a house are said to 'turn it over'; the pastry is folded over its filling.

clue.text: Harangue half of those eligible to vote

indicators.note: keeping half of the word means its first five letters are dropped

parts.note: the electorate is everyone entitled to vote

explanation.surface: Lecturing half the voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps the back half of ELECTORATE, dropping ELECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To harangue is to make a long, pompous speech, to sermonise.

clue.text: Queen (possessing mature years) is excited by desire

indicators.note: the Queen possessing something holds it within her

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth
age means old age, mature years

explanation.surface: The elderly monarch is still thrilled by passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possessing' marks a container; ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword's usual Queen, and the brackets just keep the surface tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and longing to do something, full of desire.

clue.text: Trade raised clawed feet

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: paws are an animal's clawed feet

explanation.surface: An animal deal: raising a paw to shake on it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' turns PAWS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade is to exchange one thing for another.

clue.text: Duck out of drama about lines

indicators.note: about means around or in a mixed state, so the letters are turned around into a new order

parts.note: L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: Someone ducks out of a play because of the dialogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like a verb meaning dodge; it is the bird. 'about' shuffles DRAMA with LL; 'out of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is the common wild duck, the drake with a green head.

clue.text: Power and salary retains attorney

indicators.note: a pay packet that retains something keeps it inside

parts.note: a wage is pay, a salary
ATT is an abbreviation for attorney

explanation.surface: A lawyer kept on retainer gives influence and a good income.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retains' marks a container and also plays on retaining a lawyer; ATT is a standard abbreviation for attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical power is measured in watts, and the total rating is the wattage.

clue.text: Warning — pie is fermenting -that's amazing

indicators.note: fermenting things bubble and churn, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A cautionary notice that a pie is going off, presented as a marvel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fermenting' rearranges WARNING, PIE and IS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that inspires awe is astonishing and wonderful.
